```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap, HashSet};
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, Ordering};
use std::thread;
use std::time::Duration;

use crate::config;
use crate::log::{loge, logi, logw};
use crate::mode::Candidate;
use crate::procfs;
use crate::state::StateWriter;
use crate::sys::fs as raw_fs;
use crate::sys::page;
use crate::sys::wait;
use crate::sys::{Pid, process, signal};
use crate::system::{self, SystemInfo};
use crate::targets::{ModuleInfo, Target};
use crate::trace::{State, Tracee};

pub const MODULE_ID: &str = "zygisknextsu";
pub const VERSION: &str = env!("ZNN_VERSION");

const SHUTDOWN_RELEASE_BUDGET_MS: u64 = 800;
const PROC_IDLE_SLEEP_MS: u64 = 25;

static RESCAN: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);
static SHUTDOWN: AtomicBool = AtomicBool::new(false);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Tracking {
    Kernel,
    Ptrace,
    Proc,
    Late,
}

impl Tracking {
    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Tracking::Kernel => "kernel",
            Tracking::Ptrace => "ptrace",
            Tracking::Proc => "proc",
            Tracking::Late => "late",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct Daemon {
    pub targets: Vec<Target>,
    pub modules: BTreeMap<String, ModuleInfo>,
    pub system: SystemInfo,
    pub started_at_ticks: u64,
    pub loader64: PathBuf,
    pub loader32: PathBuf,
    pub module_dir: PathBuf,
    pub state: StateWriter,
    pub kernel: Option<crate::kernel::KernelTracker>,
    pub mode: Tracking,
    pub requested_mode: String,
    pub tracees: HashMap<Pid, Tracee>,
    pub done: HashSet<Pid>,
    pub ignored: HashSet<Pid>,
    pub candidates: HashMap<Pid, Candidate>,
    pub yielded: HashSet<Pid>,
    pub deferred: HashMap<Pid, u64>,
    pub recheck: HashMap<Pid, u64>,
    pub ignored_rescans: u32,
    pub last_allocated_pid: Option<Pid>,
    pub proc_scan_active: bool,
    pub last_rescan_ms: Option<u64>,
    pub last_zygisk_check_ms: u64,
    pub last_late_sweep_ms: u64,
    pub last_state_write_ms: u64,
}

impl Daemon {
    pub fn new(module_dir: PathBuf) -> Self {
        // Log before anything that can fail or block: a daemon that dies or
        // stalls during startup must not do so silently.
        logi!("ZNNext {VERSION} starting");

        let requested_mode = config::effective().mode;

        let mut daemon = Self {
            targets: Vec::new(),
            modules: BTreeMap::new(),
            system: SystemInfo::default(),
            started_at_ticks: procfs::start_time_ticks(std::process::id() as Pid).unwrap_or(0),
            loader64: module_dir.join("lib64").join("libzn_loader.so"),
            loader32: module_dir.join("lib").join("libzn_loader.so"),
            module_dir,
            state: StateWriter::default(),
            kernel: None,
            mode: Tracking::Ptrace,
            requested_mode: requested_mode.clone(),
            tracees: HashMap::new(),
            done: HashSet::new(),
            ignored: HashSet::new(),
            candidates: HashMap::new(),
            yielded: HashSet::new(),
            deferred: HashMap::new(),
            recheck: HashMap::new(),
            ignored_rescans: 0,
            last_allocated_pid: None,
            proc_scan_active: false,
            last_rescan_ms: None,
            last_zygisk_check_ms: 0,
            last_late_sweep_ms: 0,
            last_state_write_ms: 0,
        };

        daemon.system = system::collect();
        daemon.check_loaders();
        signal::set_handler(signal::SIGHUP, on_sighup);
        //`--ctl exit` and `--ctl restart` end us with SIGTERM, and a tracee that
        //is parked on an entry breakpoint must not be left holding it
        signal::set_handler(signal::SIGTERM, on_sigterm);

        daemon.collect_targets();
        daemon.restore_processes();
        logi!("collected {} zn modules", daemon.targets.len());

        let kernel_early = requested_mode == config::MODE_KERNEL
            || (requested_mode == config::MODE_AUTO && crate::mode::monitor_present());
        if kernel_early {
            daemon.start_kernel_tracker();
        }

        daemon.select_mode();
        daemon
    }

    pub fn run(&mut self) -> ! {
        self.write_state_snapshot();
        self.last_state_write_ms = procfs::now_ms();

        loop {
            if SHUTDOWN.swap(false, Ordering::SeqCst) {
                logi!("shutting down: releasing the tracees we are holding");
                self.write_state_snapshot();
                let deadline = procfs::now_ms() + SHUTDOWN_RELEASE_BUDGET_MS;
                while !self.release_tracees() && procfs::now_ms() < deadline {
                    thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(25));
                }
                for (pid, tracee) in &self.tracees {
                    if tracee.state != State::Traced {
                        logw!("pid {pid} does not stop; its entry breakpoint is left in place");
                    }
                }
                break;
            }

            if RESCAN.swap(false, Ordering::SeqCst) {
                self.collect_targets();
                self.apply_requested_mode();
                self.last_rescan_ms = Some(procfs::now_ms());
                self.state.dirty = true;
                logi!("rescanned znn targets ({})", self.targets.len());
            }

            match self.mode {
                Tracking::Kernel => self.poll_kernel(),
                Tracking::Proc => self.poll_processes(),
                Tracking::Late => {
                    if self.kernel.is_some() {
                        self.poll_kernel();
                    } else {
                        self.poll_processes();
                    }
                    self.sweep_late_targets();
                    self.retry_deferred();
                }
                Tracking::Ptrace => {
                    let now = procfs::now_ms();
                    if self.requested_mode == config::MODE_AUTO
                        && now - self.last_zygisk_check_ms >= 5000
                    {
                        self.last_zygisk_check_ms = now;
                        if crate::mode::monitor_present() && self.hand_over_init() {
                            self.start_kernel_tracker();
                            logw!(
                                "another Zygisk-family loader is running; yielded init and switched to late mode (deferring to it)"
                            );
                            self.mode = Tracking::Late;
                            self.state.dirty = true;
                        }
                    }
                }
            }

            self.reap_traces();
            self.expire_pending();
            self.recheck_pending();

            let now = procfs::now_ms();
            if self
                .last_rescan_ms
                .is_none_or(|last_rescan| now - last_rescan >= 5000)
            {
                self.collect_targets();
                self.last_rescan_ms = Some(now);
                self.state.dirty = true;
                if self.mode == Tracking::Kernel
                    || (self.mode == Tracking::Late && self.kernel.is_some())
                {
                    self.prune_kernel_bookkeeping();
                    self.upgrade_kernel_sources();
                }
                if self.mode == Tracking::Late {
                    self.prune_deferred();
                }
                self.recheck.retain(|pid, _| procfs::is_alive(*pid));
            }
            if self.state.dirty
                && (now - self.last_state_write_ms >= 2000 || self.last_state_write_ms == 0)
            {
                self.write_state_snapshot();
                self.state.dirty = false;
                self.last_state_write_ms = now;
            }

            thread::sleep(match self.mode {
                Tracking::Proc if self.proc_scan_active => Duration::from_millis(2),
                Tracking::Proc => Duration::from_millis(PROC_IDLE_SLEEP_MS),
                Tracking::Late if self.kernel.is_some() => Duration::from_millis(1),
                Tracking::Late if self.proc_scan_active => Duration::from_millis(2),
                Tracking::Late => Duration::from_millis(PROC_IDLE_SLEEP_MS),
                Tracking::Kernel | Tracking::Ptrace => Duration::from_millis(1),
            });
        }

        process::exit_now(0)
    }

    fn check_loaders(&mut self) {
        let mut unreadable = 0;
        for path in [&self.loader64, &self.loader32] {
            if !raw_fs::access(path, raw_fs::R_OK) {
                match fs::metadata(path) {
                    Ok(_) => loge!("loader {} not readable", path.display()),
                    Err(error) => loge!("loader {} not readable: {error}", path.display()),
                }
                unreadable += 1;
                continue;
            }
            match crate::sys::fs::lgetxattr(path, "security.selinux") {
                Ok(label) => logi!(
                    "loader {} label {}",
                    path.display(),
                    String::from_utf8_lossy(&label)
                ),
                Err(error) => loge!(
                    "loader {}: cannot read selinux label: {error}",
                    path.display()
                ),
            }
        }
        if unreadable > 0 {
            self.state.status_reason = "cannot read the loader".to_owned();
        }

        let page_size = page::size();
        for path in [&self.loader64, &self.loader32] {
            let Some(align) = crate::elf::min_load_align(path) else {
                continue;
            };
            if align < page_size {
                loge!(
                    "loader {} is only {align}-byte aligned, but this device uses {page_size}-byte pages",
                    path.display()
                );
                self.state.status_reason = format!("loader not {} KB aligned", page_size / 1024);
            }
        }

        if let Ok(cap) = fs::read_to_string("/sys/fs/selinux/policy_capabilities/memfd_class")
            && cap.trim() == "1"
        {
            logw!(
                "this policy enables memfd_class: memfds are labelled with the creating domain, so \
                 the module policy may need a `memfd_file` rule for non-app targets"
            );
        }
    }

    fn reap_traces(&mut self) {
        loop {
            match wait::waitpid(-1, wait::WALL | wait::WNOHANG) {
                Ok(Some((pid, status))) => self.handle_event(pid, status),
                Ok(None) => break,
                Err(error) => {
                    if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted {
                        continue;
                    }
                    if error.raw_os_error() == Some(wait::ECHILD) {
                        break;
                    }
                    loge!("waitpid failed: {error}");
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }
}

extern "C" fn on_sighup(_signal: i32) {
    RESCAN.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
}

extern "C" fn on_sigterm(_signal: i32) {
    SHUTDOWN.store(true, Ordering::SeqCst);
}
```

```rs
use std::fs::File;
use std::os::unix::fs::FileExt;
use std::path::Path;

use object::elf::{
    EM_386, EM_AARCH64, EM_ARM, EM_RISCV, EM_X86_64, ET_DYN, FileHeader32, FileHeader64, FileType,
    Machine,
};
use object::read::elf::FileHeader as ElfFileHeader;
use object::{Endianness, FileKind, Object, ObjectKind, ObjectSegment, ObjectSymbol};

use crate::arch::Arch;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct ElfHeader {
    pub is_64: bool,
    pub kind: FileType,
    pub machine: Machine,
    pub entry: u64,
}

impl ElfHeader {
    pub fn is_position_independent(&self) -> bool {
        self.kind == ET_DYN
    }
}

fn parse_header(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ElfHeader> {
    match FileKind::parse(bytes).ok()? {
        FileKind::Elf64 => header_of::<FileHeader64<Endianness>>(bytes),
        FileKind::Elf32 => header_of::<FileHeader32<Endianness>>(bytes),
        _ => None,
    }
}

fn header_of<H: ElfFileHeader>(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<ElfHeader> {
    let header = H::parse(bytes).ok()?;
    let endian = header.endian().ok()?;
    Some(ElfHeader {
        is_64: header.is_type_64(),
        kind: header.e_type(endian),
        machine: header.e_machine(endian),
        entry: header.e_entry(endian).into(),
    })
}

pub fn header_of_file(path: &Path) -> Option<ElfHeader> {
    let file = File::open(path).ok()?;
    let mut buffer = [0u8; 64];
    let read = file.read_at(&mut buffer, 0).ok()?;
    parse_header(&buffer[..read])
}

pub fn min_load_align(path: &Path) -> Option<u64> {
    let bytes = std::fs::read(path).ok()?;
    let file = object::File::parse(&*bytes).ok()?;
    let mut smallest: Option<u64> = None;
    for segment in file.segments() {
        let align = segment.align();
        if align <= 1 {
            continue;
        }
        smallest = Some(smallest.map_or(align, |current| current.min(align)));
    }
    smallest
}

pub fn arch_of(header: &ElfHeader) -> Arch {
    if header.is_64 {
        match header.machine {
            EM_AARCH64 => Arch::Arm64,
            EM_X86_64 => Arch::X86_64,
            EM_RISCV => Arch::Riscv64,
            _ => Arch::Unknown,
        }
    } else {
        match header.machine {
            EM_ARM => Arch::Arm32,
            EM_386 => Arch::X86,
            _ => Arch::Unknown,
        }
    }
}

pub fn symbol_address(path: &Path, base: usize, symbol: &str) -> usize {
    let Ok(bytes) = std::fs::read(path) else {
        return 0;
    };
    let Ok(file) = object::File::parse(&*bytes) else {
        return 0;
    };
    let address = file
        .dynamic_symbols()
        .chain(file.symbols())
        .find(|candidate| {
            !candidate.is_undefined() && candidate.name().is_ok_and(|name| name == symbol)
        })
        .and_then(|candidate| usize::try_from(candidate.address()).ok());
    match address {
        Some(value) if file.kind() == ObjectKind::Dynamic => base.wrapping_add(value),
        Some(value) => value,
        None => 0,
    }
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.

 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or

 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fs::{self, OpenOptions};
use std::io::{self, Write};
use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

pub fn replace_file(target: &Path, contents: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
    let temporary = temporary_path(target);
    match fs::remove_file(&temporary) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {}
        Err(error) => return Err(error),
    }
    match write_new(&temporary, contents) {
        Ok(()) => {}
        Err(error) => {
            let _ = fs::remove_file(&temporary);
            return Err(error);
        }
    }
    if let Err(error) = fs::rename(&temporary, target) {
        let _ = fs::remove_file(&temporary);
        return Err(error);
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub fn temporary_path(target: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    let mut name = target.as_os_str().to_owned();
    name.push(".tmp");
    PathBuf::from(name)
}

fn write_new(path: &Path, contents: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> {
    let mut file = OpenOptions::new()
        .write(true)
        .create_new(true)
        .mode(0o644)
        .custom_flags(libc::O_NOFOLLOW)
        .open(path)?;
    file.write_all(contents)?;
    file.sync_all()
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fmt;

use crate::daemon::Daemon;
use crate::kernel_bpf::BpfTracker;
use crate::kernel_connector::ConnectorTracker;
use crate::kernel_fanotify::FanotifyTracker;
use crate::kernel_kpm::KpmTracker;
use crate::kernel_tracefs::TracefsTracker;
use crate::log::{logi, logw};
use crate::procfs;
use crate::sys::Pid;
use crate::sys::poll;
use crate::targets::Target;

pub const POLL_TIMEOUT_MS: i32 = 20;
const RECHECK_TIMEOUT_MS: u64 = 150;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum EventKind {
    Exec,
    Fork,
    Exit,
}

impl EventKind {
    #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "64")]
    pub fn from_raw(raw: u32) -> Option<Self> {
        match raw {
            0 => Some(EventKind::Exec),
            1 => Some(EventKind::Fork),
            2 => Some(EventKind::Exit),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn as_str(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            EventKind::Exec => "exec",
            EventKind::Fork => "fork",
            EventKind::Exit => "exit",
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct KernelEvent {
    pub kind: EventKind,
    pub pid: Pid,
    pub uid: u32,
    pub ppid: Pid,
    pub comm: [u8; 16],
    pub filename: Option<String>,
    pub pre_exec: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct KernelTracker {
    tracefs: Option<TracefsTracker>,
    connector: Option<ConnectorTracker>,
    bpf: Option<BpfTracker>,
    fanotify: Option<FanotifyTracker>,
    kpm: Option<KpmTracker>,
    bpf_pending: bool,
}

impl KernelTracker {
    pub fn start(targets: &[Target]) -> Option<Self> {
        let tracefs = match TracefsTracker::start() {
            Ok(tracker) => {
                logi!(
                    "kernel tracking: tracefs source ready at {} (sched exec/exit events)",
                    tracker.instance_path().display()
                );
                Some(tracker)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                logw!("kernel tracking: tracefs source unavailable: {error}");
                None
            }
        };
        let connector = match ConnectorTracker::start() {
            Ok(tracker) => {
                logi!("kernel tracking: proc connector source ready (fork/exec/exit)");
                Some(tracker)
            }
            Err(error) => {
                logw!("kernel tracking: proc connector unavailable: {error}");
                None
            }
        };
        let booted =
            crate::sys::prop::system_property("sys.boot_completed").as_deref() == Some("1");
        let (bpf, bpf_pending) = if booted {
            (start_bpf(), false)
        } else {
            logi!("kernel tracking: eBPF source held back until boot completes");
            (None, true)
        };
        let fanotify = match FanotifyTracker::start(targets) {
            Ok(tracker) => Some(tracker),
            Err(error) => {
                logw!("kernel tracking: fanotify source unavailable: {error}");
                None
            }
        };
        let kpm = match KpmTracker::start() {
            Ok(tracker) => Some(tracker),
            Err(error) => {
                logw!("kernel tracking: KernelPatch znn source unavailable: {error}");
                None
            }
        };

        if tracefs.is_none()
            && connector.is_none()
            && bpf.is_none()
            && fanotify.is_none()
            && kpm.is_none()
        {
            return None;
        }
        Some(Self {
            tracefs,
            connector,
            bpf,
            fanotify,
            kpm,
            bpf_pending,
        })
    }

    pub fn upgrade(&mut self) {
        if !self.bpf_pending {
            return;
        }
        if crate::sys::prop::system_property("sys.boot_completed").as_deref() != Some("1") {
            return;
        }
        if let Some(bpf) = start_bpf() {
            self.bpf = Some(bpf);
            self.bpf_pending = false;
        }
    }

    pub fn description(&self) -> String {
        let mut sources = Vec::new();
        if self.tracefs.is_some() {
            sources.push("tracefs sched exec/exit events");
        }
        if self.connector.is_some() {
            sources.push("proc connector fork/exec/exit events");
        }
        if self.bpf.is_some() {
            sources.push("eBPF exec events");
        } else if self.bpf_pending {
            sources.push("eBPF source pending boot completion");
        }
        if self.fanotify.is_some() {
            sources.push("fanotify exec events");
        }
        if self.kpm.is_some() {
            sources.push("KernelPatch znn exec records");
        }
        if sources.is_empty() {
            return "no kernel event source".to_owned();
        }
        sources.join(" and ")
    }

    pub fn poll(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        let mut descriptors = Vec::new();
        if let Some(tracefs) = &self.tracefs {
            descriptors.push(tracefs.descriptor());
        }
        if let Some(bpf) = &self.bpf {
            descriptors.push(bpf.descriptor());
        }
        if let Some(connector) = &self.connector {
            descriptors.push(connector.descriptor());
        }
        if let Some(fanotify) = &self.fanotify {
            descriptors.push(fanotify.descriptor());
        }
        let _ = poll::poll_readable(&descriptors, POLL_TIMEOUT_MS);

        if let Some(tracefs) = &mut self.tracefs {
            tracefs.drain(events);
        }
        if let Some(bpf) = &mut self.bpf {
            bpf.drain(events);
        }
        if let Some(connector) = &mut self.connector {
            connector.drain(events);
        }
        if let Some(fanotify) = &mut self.fanotify {
            fanotify.drain(events);
        }
        if let Some(kpm) = &mut self.kpm {
            kpm.drain(events);
        }
    }
}

fn start_bpf() -> Option<BpfTracker> {
    match BpfTracker::start() {
        Ok(tracker) => {
            logi!("kernel tracking: eBPF exec source ready (raw tracepoint sched_process_exec)");
            Some(tracker)
        }
        Err(error) => {
            logw!("kernel tracking: eBPF source unavailable: {error}");
            None
        }
    }
}

impl Daemon {
    pub fn start_kernel_tracker(&mut self) -> bool {
        if self.kernel.is_some() {
            return true;
        }
        let Some(tracker) = KernelTracker::start(&self.targets) else {
            return false;
        };
        logi!("tracking mode kernel: {}", tracker.description());
        self.kernel = Some(tracker);
        true
    }

    pub fn stop_kernel_tracker(&mut self) {
        if self.kernel.take().is_some() {
            logi!("kernel tracking: stopped");
        }
    }

    pub fn poll_kernel(&mut self) {
        let mut events = Vec::new();
        if let Some(tracker) = self.kernel.as_mut() {
            tracker.poll(&mut events);
        }
        for event in events {
            self.consider_kernel_event(event);
        }
    }

    fn consider_kernel_event(&mut self, event: KernelEvent) {
        let pid = event.pid;
        if pid <= 1 {
            return;
        }

        match event.kind {
            EventKind::Fork => return,
            EventKind::Exit => {
                self.candidates.remove(&pid);
                self.done.remove(&pid);
                self.ignored.remove(&pid);
                self.deferred.remove(&pid);
                self.recheck.remove(&pid);
                return;
            }
            EventKind::Exec => {}
        }

        if self.tracees.contains_key(&pid)
            || self.done.contains(&pid)
            || self.ignored.contains(&pid)
        {
            return;
        }

        if event.pre_exec {
            if procfs::foreign_tracer(pid).is_none() {
                self.defer_recheck(pid, event.filename.as_deref());
            }
            return;
        }

        let exe = procfs::read_exe_path(pid);
        if exe.is_empty() {
            if procfs::process_gone(pid) {
                self.ignored.insert(pid);
            }
            return;
        }
        let exec_path = event.filename.as_deref().filter(|name| !name.is_empty());
        let is_target = crate::targets::matches(&self.targets, &exe)
            || exec_path.is_some_and(|name| crate::targets::matches(&self.targets, name));
        if !is_target {
            self.ignored.insert(pid);
            return;
        }

        let comm = String::from_utf8_lossy(&event.comm);
        let exec_path_note = exec_path
            .map(|name| format!(" (exec path {name})"))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        logi!(
            "{exe} (pid {pid}, uid {}, ppid {}, comm {}) appeared via a {} event{exec_path_note}",
            event.uid,
            event.ppid,
            comm.trim_end_matches('\0'),
            event.kind.as_str()
        );
        self.observe_target(pid, &exe);
    }

    fn defer_recheck(&mut self, pid: Pid, exec_path: Option<&str>) {
        let exec_path = exec_path.filter(|name| !name.is_empty());
        if let Some(path) = exec_path
            && !crate::targets::matches(&self.targets, path)
        {
            self.ignored.insert(pid);
            return;
        }
        if self.recheck.contains_key(&pid) {
            return;
        }
        self.recheck
            .insert(pid, procfs::now_ms() + RECHECK_TIMEOUT_MS);
        let note = exec_path
            .map(|name| format!(" (exec path {name})"))
            .unwrap_or_default();
        logi!("pid {pid}: exec in flight{note}; rechecking in {RECHECK_TIMEOUT_MS} ms");
    }

    pub fn upgrade_kernel_sources(&mut self) {
        if let Some(tracker) = self.kernel.as_mut() {
            tracker.upgrade();
        }
    }

    pub fn prune_kernel_bookkeeping(&mut self) {
        self.done.retain(|pid| procfs::is_alive(*pid));
        self.ignored.retain(|pid| procfs::is_alive(*pid));
        self.candidates.retain(|pid, _| procfs::is_alive(*pid));
    }
}

impl fmt::Display for EventKind {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str(self.as_str())
    }
}
```

```rs
#[cfg(target_pointer_width = "64")]
mod implementation {
    use std::fmt;
    use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, RawFd};

    use aya::Ebpf;
    use aya::maps::{MapData, RingBuf};
    use aya::programs::RawTracePoint;

    use crate::kernel::{EventKind, KernelEvent};
    use crate::sys::Pid;

    const OBJECT: &[u8] = include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), "/exec.bpf.o"));
    const RING_BUFFER_MAP: &str = "EVENTS";
    const EXEC_PROGRAM: &str = "handle_exec";
    const EXEC_TRACEPOINT: &str = "sched_process_exec";
    const RECORD_SIZE: usize = 40;

    pub struct BpfTracker {
        _bpf: Ebpf,
        ring: RingBuf<MapData>,
    }

    impl fmt::Debug for BpfTracker {
        fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
            formatter.write_str("BpfTracker")
        }
    }

    impl BpfTracker {
        pub fn start() -> Result<Self, String> {
            let mut bpf = Ebpf::load(OBJECT)
                .map_err(|error| format!("cannot load the BPF object: {error}"))?;
            {
                let program: &mut RawTracePoint = bpf
                    .program_mut(EXEC_PROGRAM)
                    .ok_or_else(|| format!("the BPF object has no {EXEC_PROGRAM} program"))?
                    .try_into()
                    .map_err(|error| {
                        format!("{EXEC_PROGRAM} is not a raw tracepoint program: {error}")
                    })?;
                program
                    .load()
                    .map_err(|error| format!("the verifier rejected {EXEC_PROGRAM}: {error}"))?;
                program
                    .attach(EXEC_TRACEPOINT)
                    .map_err(|error| format!("cannot attach {EXEC_TRACEPOINT}: {error}"))?;
            }

            let map = bpf
                .take_map(RING_BUFFER_MAP)
                .ok_or_else(|| format!("the BPF object has no {RING_BUFFER_MAP} map"))?;
            let ring = RingBuf::try_from(map)
                .map_err(|error| format!("{RING_BUFFER_MAP} is not a ring buffer: {error}"))?;
            Ok(Self { _bpf: bpf, ring })
        }

        pub fn descriptor(&self) -> RawFd {
            self.ring.as_raw_fd()
        }

        pub fn drain(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
            while let Some(record) = self.ring.next() {
                let bytes: &[u8] = &record;
                if let Some(event) = decode(bytes) {
                    events.push(event);
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn decode(record: &[u8]) -> Option<KernelEvent> {
        if record.len() < RECORD_SIZE {
            return None;
        }
        Some(KernelEvent {
            kind: EventKind::from_raw(read_u32(record, 0)?)?,
            pid: read_u32(record, 4)? as Pid,
            uid: read_u32(record, 12)?,
            ppid: read_u32(record, 16)? as Pid,
            comm: record[24..40].try_into().ok()?,
            filename: None,
            pre_exec: false,
        })
    }

    fn read_u32(bytes: &[u8], offset: usize) -> Option<u32> {
        Some(u32::from_ne_bytes(
            bytes.get(offset..offset + 4)?.try_into().ok()?,
        ))
    }
}

#[cfg(not(target_pointer_width = "64"))]
mod implementation {
    use std::os::fd::RawFd;

    use crate::kernel::KernelEvent;

    #[derive(Debug)]
    pub struct BpfTracker;

    impl BpfTracker {
        pub fn start() -> Result<Self, String> {
            Err("this target is 32-bit, so only the proc connector source is available".to_owned())
        }

        pub fn descriptor(&self) -> RawFd {
            -1
        }

        pub fn drain(&mut self, _events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {}
    }
}

pub use implementation::BpfTracker;
```

```rs
/*

 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License

use std::fmt;
use std::io;
use std::os::fd::RawFd;

use crate::kernel::{EventKind, KernelEvent};
use crate::log::logw;
use crate::sys::netlink::{Connector, ProcEvent};

pub struct ConnectorTracker {
    connector: Connector,
    pending: Vec<ProcEvent>,
    reported_error: bool,
}

impl fmt::Debug for ConnectorTracker {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str("ConnectorTracker")
    }
}

impl ConnectorTracker {
    pub fn start() -> io::Result<Self> {
        Ok(Self {
            connector: Connector::open()?,
            pending: Vec::new(),
            reported_error: false,
        })
    }

    pub fn descriptor(&self) -> RawFd {
        self.connector.descriptor()
    }

    pub fn drain(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        self.pending.clear();
        if let Err(error) = self.connector.drain(&mut self.pending) {
            if !self.reported_error {
                self.reported_error = true;
                logw!("kernel tracking: proc connector subscription failed: {error}");
            }
            return;
        }

        for event in &self.pending {
            let (kind, pid, ppid) = match *event {
                ProcEvent::Fork { parent, child } => (EventKind::Fork, child, parent),
                ProcEvent::Exec { pid } => (EventKind::Exec, pid, 0),
                ProcEvent::Exit { pid } => (EventKind::Exit, pid, 0),
            };
            events.push(KernelEvent {
                kind,
                pid,
                uid: 0,
                ppid,
                comm: [0; 16],
                filename: None,
                pre_exec: false,
            });
        }
    }
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fmt;
use std::fs;
use std::os::fd::RawFd;
use std::path::Path;

use crate::kernel::{EventKind, KernelEvent};
use crate::log::{logi, logw};
use crate::sys::fanotify::{Events, FAN_OPEN_EXEC, Fanotify};
use crate::sys::fs as raw_fs;
use crate::targets::Target;

const READ_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 8192;
const MAX_PENDING: usize = 1 << 16;

pub struct FanotifyTracker {
    fanotify: Fanotify,
    pending: Vec<u8>,
    reported_error: bool,
}

impl fmt::Debug for FanotifyTracker {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str("FanotifyTracker")
    }
}

impl FanotifyTracker {
    pub fn start(targets: &[Target]) -> Result<Self, String> {
        let fanotify =
            Fanotify::init().map_err(|error| format!("fanotify_init failed: {error}"))?;

        let mut marked = 0usize;
        for target in targets {
            if target.by_name {
                continue;
            }
            match fanotify.add_path_mark(Path::new(&target.value), FAN_OPEN_EXEC) {
                Ok(()) => marked += 1,
                Err(error) => logw!(
                    "kernel tracking: cannot mark {} for fanotify exec events: {error}",
                    target.value
                ),
            }
        }
        if marked == 0 {
            return Err("no fanotify path targets".to_owned());
        }
        logi!("kernel tracking: fanotify exec source ready on {marked} path target(s)");
        Ok(Self {
            fanotify,
            pending: Vec::new(),
            reported_error: false,
        })
    }

    pub fn descriptor(&self) -> RawFd {
        self.fanotify.descriptor()
    }

    pub fn drain(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        let mut buffer = [0u8; READ_BUFFER_SIZE];
        loop {
            match self.fanotify.read_event(&mut buffer) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(read) => {
                    self.pending.extend_from_slice(&buffer[..read]);
                    let consumed = emit_records(&self.pending, events);
                    self.pending.drain(..consumed);
                }
                Err(error) => {
                    if !self.reported_error {
                        self.reported_error = true;
                        logw!("kernel tracking: fanotify event read failed: {error}");
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
        if self.pending.len() > MAX_PENDING {
            self.pending.clear();
        }
    }
}

fn emit_records(pending: &[u8], events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) -> usize {
    let mut records = Events::new(pending);
    for (pid, fd, _mask) in &mut records {
        if pid > 0 {
            let filename = fs::read_link(format!("/proc/self/fd/{fd}"))
                .ok()
                .map(|path| path.to_string_lossy().into_owned());
            events.push(KernelEvent {
                kind: EventKind::Exec,
                pid,
                uid: 0,
                ppid: 0,
                comm: [0; 16],
                filename,
                pre_exec: true,
            });
        }
        if fd >= 0 {
            raw_fs::close(fd);
        }
    }
    records.consumed()
}
```

`daemon/src/kernel_kpm.rs`:

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use crate::kernel::{EventKind, KernelEvent};
use crate::log::logi;
use crate::sys::Pid;
use crate::sys::kpm;

const MAX_ROUNDS: usize = 4;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct KpmTracker {
    since_seq: u64,
    buffer: Vec<u8>,
}

impl KpmTracker {
    pub fn start() -> Result<Self, String> {
        let mut buffer = vec![0u8; kpm::MAX_PAYLOAD];
        match kpm::read_records(&mut buffer, 0) {
            Ok(_) => {
                logi!("kernel tracking: KernelPatch znn channel ready");
                Ok(Self {
                    since_seq: 0,
                    buffer,
                })
            }
            Err(error) => Err(error.to_string()),
        }
    }

    pub fn drain(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        for _ in 0..MAX_ROUNDS {
            let Ok(read) = kpm::read_records(&mut self.buffer, self.since_seq) else {
                return;
            };
            if read == 0 {
                return;
            }
            let filled = read.min(self.buffer.len());
            let mut last_seq = self.since_seq;
            let text = String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.buffer[..filled]);
            for line in text.lines() {
                let Some(record) = parse_line(line) else {
                    continue;
                };
                last_seq = last_seq.max(record.seq);
                if record.pid <= 0 {
                    continue;
                }
                events.push(KernelEvent {
                    kind: EventKind::Exec,
                    pid: record.pid,
                    uid: 0,
                    ppid: record.ppid,
                    comm: [0; 16],
                    filename: None,
                    pre_exec: true,
                });
            }
            self.since_seq = last_seq;
            if filled < self.buffer.len() {
                return;
            }
        }
    }
}

struct Record {
    seq: u64,
    pid: Pid,
    ppid: Pid,
}

fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Option<Record> {
    let mut seq = None;
    let mut pid = None;
    let mut ppid = None;
    for token in line.split_whitespace() {
        let Some((key, value)) = token.split_once('=') else {
            continue;
        };
        match key {
            "seq" => seq = value.parse().ok(),
            "pid" => pid = value.parse::<Pid>().ok(),
            "ppid" => ppid = value.parse::<Pid>().ok(),
            _ => {}
        }
    }
    Some(Record {
        seq: seq?,
        pid: pid?,
        ppid: ppid?,
    })
}
```

`daemon/src/kernel_tracefs.rs`:

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fmt;
use std::fs::{self, File};
use std::io::{self, Read};
use std::os::fd::{AsRawFd, RawFd};
use std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use crate::kernel::{EventKind, KernelEvent};
use crate::log::{logi, logw};
use crate::sys::Pid;

const TRACEFS_ROOTS: [&str; 2] = ["/sys/kernel/tracing", "/sys/kernel/debug/tracing"];
const INSTANCE: &str = "znn";
const EVENTS: [&str; 2] = ["sched_process_exec", "sched_process_exit"];
const BUFFER_SIZE_KB: u32 = 64;
const READ_BUFFER_SIZE: usize = 8192;
const MAX_TAIL_SIZE: usize = 1 << 16;

pub struct TracefsTracker {
    pipe: File,
    instance: PathBuf,
    tail: Vec<u8>,
    reported_error: bool,
    reported_loss: bool,
}

impl fmt::Debug for TracefsTracker {
    fn fmt(&self, formatter: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
        formatter.write_str("TracefsTracker")
    }
}

impl TracefsTracker {
    pub fn start() -> Result<Self, String> {
        let mut errors = Vec::new();
        for root in TRACEFS_ROOTS {
            let root = Path::new(root);
            if !root.is_dir() {
                errors.push(format!("{} is absent", root.display()));
                continue;
            }
            match Self::open(root) {
                Ok(tracker) => return Ok(tracker),
                Err(error) => errors.push(format!("{}: {error}", root.display())),
            }
        }
        Err(errors.join("; "))
    }

    fn open(root: &Path) -> io::Result<Self> {
        let instance = root.join("instances").join(INSTANCE);
        if !instance.is_dir() {
            fs::create_dir_all(&instance)?;
        }

        let events = instance.join("events").join("sched");
        for event in EVENTS {
            if let Err(error) = fs::write(events.join(event).join("enable"), "1") {
                disable(&instance);
                return Err(error);
            }
        }
        let _ = fs::write(instance.join("buffer_size_kb"), BUFFER_SIZE_KB.to_string());

        let pipe = match fs::OpenOptions::new()
            .read(true)
            .custom_flags(libc::O_NONBLOCK)
            .open(instance.join("trace_pipe"))
        {
            Ok(pipe) => pipe,
            Err(error) => {
                disable(&instance);
                return Err(error);
            }
        };
        logi!(
            "kernel tracking: tracefs instance {} listening on sched exec/exit events",
            instance.display()
        );
        Ok(Self {
            pipe,
            instance,
            tail: Vec::new(),
            reported_error: false,
            reported_loss: false,
        })
    }

    pub fn instance_path(&self) -> &Path {
        &self.instance
    }

    pub fn descriptor(&self) -> RawFd {
        self.pipe.as_raw_fd()
    }

    pub fn drain(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        let mut buffer = [0u8; READ_BUFFER_SIZE];
        loop {
            match self.pipe.read(&mut buffer) {
                Ok(0) => break,
                Ok(read) => {
                    self.tail.extend_from_slice(&buffer[..read]);
                    self.emit_lines(events);
                }
                Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::WouldBlock => break,
                Err(error) if error.kind() == io::ErrorKind::Interrupted => continue,
                Err(error) => {
                    if !self.reported_error {
                        self.reported_error = true;
                        logw!("kernel tracking: tracefs trace_pipe read failed: {error}");
                    }
                    break;
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn emit_lines(&mut self, events: &mut Vec<KernelEvent>) {
        let mut line_start = 0;
        let mut lost = false;
        for (index, byte) in self.tail.iter().enumerate() {
            if *byte != b'\n' {
                continue;
            }
            let line = String::from_utf8_lossy(&self.tail[line_start..index]);
            if is_lost_events_line(&line) {
                lost = true;
            } else if let Some(event) = parse_line(&line) {
                events.push(event);
            }
            line_start = index + 1;
        }
        self.tail.drain(..line_start);
        if self.tail.len() > MAX_TAIL_SIZE {
            self.tail.clear();
        }
        if lost {
            self.report_loss();
        }
    }

    fn report_loss(&mut self) {
        if self.reported_loss {
            return;
        }
        self.reported_loss = true;
        logw!(
            "kernel tracking: the tracefs ring buffer dropped events; a target exec may not have been seen"
        );
    }
}

impl Drop for TracefsTracker {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        disable(&self.instance);
    }
}

fn disable(instance: &Path) {
    let events = instance.join("events").join("sched");
    for event in EVENTS {
        let _ = fs::write(events.join(event).join("enable"), "0");
    }
}

fn parse_line(line: &str) -> Option<KernelEvent> {
    let (kind, fields) = match line.split_once("sched_process_exec:") {
        Some((_, fields)) => (EventKind::Exec, fields),
        None => {
            let (_, fields) = line.split_once("sched_process_exit:")?;
            (EventKind::Exit, fields)
        }
    };

    let pid = field(fields, "pid")?.parse::<Pid>().ok()?;
    let mut comm = [0u8; 16];
    if let Some(name) = field(fields, "comm").or_else(|| prefix_comm(line)) {
        let bytes = name.as_bytes();
        let length = bytes.len().min(comm.len());
        comm[..length].copy_from_slice(&bytes[..length]);
    }

    Some(KernelEvent {
        kind,
        pid,
        uid: 0,
        ppid: 0,
        comm,
        filename: field(fields, "filename").map(str::to_owned),
        pre_exec: false,
    })
}

fn field<'a>(fields: &'a str, key: &str) -> Option<&'a str> {
    fields.split_whitespace().find_map(|token| {
        let (name, value) = token.split_once('=')?;
        (name == key).then_some(value)
    })
}

fn prefix_comm(line: &str) -> Option<&str> {
    let (prefix, _) = line.trim_start().split_once(' ')?;
    let (comm, _) = prefix.rsplit_once('-')?;
    (!comm.is_empty()).then_some(comm)
}

fn is_lost_events_line(line: &str) -> bool {
    line.contains("[LOST ") && line.contains(" EVENTS]")
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn parses_an_exec_line() {
        let line = "sh-1234  [002] ....  4567.890123: sched_process_exec: filename=/system/bin/app_process64 pid=1234 old_pid=1234";
        let event = parse_line(line).expect("exec line parses");
        assert_eq!(event.kind, EventKind::Exec);
        assert_eq!(event.pid, 1234);
        assert_eq!(event.filename.as_deref(), Some("/system/bin/app_process64"));
        assert_eq!(&event.comm[..2], b"sh");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_an_exit_line() {
        let line = "          <idle>-0     [000] d.h.  4567.890123: sched_process_exit: comm=swapper/0 pid=42 prio=120";
        let event = parse_line(line).expect("exit line parses");
        assert_eq!(event.kind, EventKind::Exit);
        assert_eq!(event.pid, 42);
        assert_eq!(event.filename, None);
        assert_eq!(&event.comm[..7], b"swapper");
    }

    #[test]
    fn ignores_other_lines() {
        assert!(parse_line("sh-1234 [002] .... 4567.890123: sched_switch: prev_comm=sh").is_none());
        assert!(parse_line("").is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn recognizes_lost_event_markers() {
        assert!(is_lost_events_line("CPU:1 [LOST 8 EVENTS]"));
        assert!(is_lost_events_line("CPU:0 [LOST 123 EVENTS]"));
        assert!(!is_lost_events_line(
            "sh-1234 [002] .... 4567.890123: sched_process_exec: pid=1234"
        ));
    }
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

use machikado_rs::{FileEntry, verify};

use crate::daemon::MODULE_ID;

use crate::mazoku::ORG_PUBLIC_KEY;

const SIGNED_FILES: [&str; 9] = [
    "bin/znnd",
    "emulated-soft-reboot.sh",
    "lib/libzn_loader.so",
    "lib64/libzn_loader.so",
    "mazoku",
    "module.prop.orig",
    "post-fs-data.sh",
    "late-load.sh",
    "sepolicy.rule",
];

fn load_entry(path: &Path, relative_path: &str) -> Result<FileEntry, String> {
    let content = fs::read(path).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    Ok(FileEntry {
        relative_path: relative_path.to_owned(),
        content,
    })
}

fn load_webroot(dir: &Path, prefix: &str, entries: &mut Vec<FileEntry>) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut children = Vec::new();
    for child in fs::read_dir(dir).map_err(|error| error.to_string())? {
        children.push(child.map_err(|error| error.to_string())?);
    }
    children.sort_by_key(|child| child.file_name());

    for child in children {
        let file_type = child.file_type().map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
        let relative_path = format!("{prefix}/{}", child.file_name().to_string_lossy());
        if file_type.is_dir() {
            load_webroot(&child.path(), &relative_path, entries)?;
        } else if file_type.is_file() {
            entries.push(load_entry(&child.path(), &relative_path)?);
        }
    }
    Ok(())
}

pub(crate) fn verify_module(module_dir: &Path) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut entries = Vec::new();
    for relative_path in SIGNED_FILES {
        entries.push(load_entry(&module_dir.join(relative_path), relative_path)?);
    }
    load_webroot(&module_dir.join("webroot"), "webroot", &mut entries)?;
    entries.sort_by(|a, b| a.relative_path.cmp(&b.relative_path));

    let machikado = fs::read(module_dir.join("machikado")).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;
    let mazoku = fs::read(module_dir.join("mazoku")).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?;

    let (ok, error) = verify(&machikado, &mazoku, &entries, MODULE_ID, &ORG_PUBLIC_KEY);
    if ok {
        Ok(())
    } else {
        Err(error.map_or_else(
            || "signature verification failed".to_owned(),
            |error| error.to_string(),
        ))
    }
}

pub(crate) fn restore_prop(module_dir: &Path) {
    let original = module_dir.join("module.prop.orig");
    if original.is_file() {
        let _ = fs::copy(&original, module_dir.join("module.prop"));
    }
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

#![deny(unsafe_code)]
mod arch;
mod companion;
mod config;
mod ctl;
mod daemon;
mod elf;
mod fileio;
mod kernel;
mod kernel_bpf;
mod kernel_connector;
mod kernel_fanotify;
mod kernel_kpm;
mod kernel_tracefs;
mod log;
mod machikado;
mod maps;
mod mazoku;
mod mode;
mod paths;
mod plan;
mod procfs;
mod ptrace_ops;
mod state;
mod sys;
mod system;
mod targets;
mod trace;
mod zn;

fn main() {
    let matches = ctl::command().get_matches();

    if let Some(arguments) = ctl::ctl_arguments(&matches) {
        std::process::exit(ctl::ctl_main(&arguments));
    }

    let module_dir = ctl::module_dir(&matches).unwrap_or_else(ctl::module_dir_of_self);

    if let Err(error) = machikado::verify_module(&module_dir) {
        crate::log::loge!("module verification failed: {error}");
        machikado::restore_prop(&module_dir);
        std::process::exit(1);
    }

    let deadline = std::time::Instant::now() + std::time::Duration::from_millis(3000);
    let mut reported = false;
    while let Some(pid) = procfs::find_daemon_pid(None) {
        if !reported {
            crate::log::logi!("waiting for the previous daemon ({pid}) to exit");
            reported = true;
        }
        if std::time::Instant::now() >= deadline {
            crate::log::loge!(
                "an daemon ({pid}) is already running, refusing to start a second instance"
            );
            std::process::exit(1);
        }
        std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(100));
    }

    daemon::Daemon::new(module_dir).run();
}
```

```rs
/*
 * This file is part of ZNNext.
 *
 * ZNNext is free software: you can redistribute it and/or modify
 * it under the terms of the GNU General Public License as published by
 * the Free Software Foundation, either version 3 of the License, or
 * (at your option) any later version.
 *
 * ZNNext is distributed in the hope that it will be useful,
 * but WITHOUT ANY WARRANTY; without even the implied warranty of
 * MERCHANTABILITY or FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE. See the
 * GNU General Public License for more details.
 *
 * You should have received a copy of the GNU General Public License
 * along with ZNNext. If not, see <https://www.gnu.org/licenses/>.
 *
 * Copyright (C) 2026 VeryBaaad <verybaaad@outlook.com>
 */

use std::fs;

use crate::sys::Pid;

pub const PROT_READ: u8 = 0x1;
pub const PROT_WRITE: u8 = 0x2;
pub const PROT_EXEC: u8 = 0x4;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct MapEntry {
    pub start: usize,
    pub end: usize,
    pub offset: usize,
    pub perms: u8,
    pub path: String,
}

impl MapEntry {
    pub fn contains(&self, address: usize) -> bool {
        address >= self.start && address < self.end
    }
}

pub fn parse_for_pid(pid: Pid) -> Vec<MapEntry> {
    parse_path(&format!("/proc/{pid}/maps"))
}

pub fn parse_path(path: &str) -> Vec<MapEntry> {
    let Ok(contents) = fs::read(path) else {
        return Vec::new();
    };
    contents
        .split(|byte| *byte == b'\n')
        .filter_map(parse_line)
        .collect()
}

fn parse_line(line: &[u8]) -> Option<MapEntry> {
    let mut fields = line.splitn(6, |byte| *byte == b' ');
    let range = fields.next()?;
    let perms = fields.next()?;
    let offset = fields.next()?;
    fields.next()?; // device
    fields.next()?; // inode
    let path = fields.next().unwrap_or_default();
    let path = match path.iter().position(|byte| !byte.is_ascii_whitespace()) {
        Some(start) => &path[start..],
        None => &path[..0],
    };

    let dash = range.iter().position(|byte| *byte == b'-')?;
    let (start, end) = (&range[..dash], &range[dash + 1..]);
    if perms.len() < 4 {
        return None;
    }

    let mut decoded = 0;
    if perms[0] == b'r' {
        decoded |= PROT_READ;
    }
    if perms[1] == b'w' {
        decoded |= PROT_WRITE;
    }
    if perms[2] == b'x' {
        decoded |= PROT_EXEC;
    }

    Some(MapEntry {
        start: address(start)?,
        end: address(end)?,
        offset: address(offset)?,
        perms: decoded,
        path: String::from_utf8_lossy(path)
            .trim_end_matches(['\n', '\r'])
            .to_owned(),
    })
}

/// Parse one hexadecimal column of a maps line.
fn address(field: &[u8]) -> Option<usize> {
    usize::from_str_radix(std::str::from_utf8(field).ok()?, 16).ok()
}
```
